subject: CloudMetrics — Dedicated pool sizing, throughput SLA and GPU mix
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@cloudmetrics.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Anand Patel <anand.patel@cloudmetrics.com>, CloudMetrics Procurement <procure@cloudmetrics.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated pool sizing & GPU options — follow up

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re close to an internal decision but need clearer guidance on two things before procurement signs a PO:

1) Practical perf/$ tradeoffs between A100, H100 and L40S for our primary workloads (chat+retrieval generation at 2–4k context and large-batch embedding runs). Memory matters for our embeddings job (batch size 512).
2) What committed sizing (GPUs and throughput guarantees) we should buy to hit a 95th percentile token latency SLA of ~180ms for chat and keep embedding batch throughput >= 6,000 vectors/hr.

Procurement is pushing for a single monthly committed contract (6 months) and wants to see the price matrix + example billing math. They asked whether we can get a 20–25% discount for that term if we commit to a mixed pool.

Can you send a proposal and pricing matrix by EOD Friday? Attaching the cost center code in a separate note.

—Elena
Head of Platform Engineering, CloudMetrics
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@cloudmetrics.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 11:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing & GPU options — follow up

Elena — thanks for the clear ask. I pulled together an initial sizing + pricing matrix (attached) and some engineering notes below so your procurement and infra teams have what they need. High-level summary up front:

- Recommendation: 24-slot committed pool with a hybrid mix: 14 x A100 80GB + 10 x L40S. Why: A100s give consistent perf/$ for generative chat with 2–4k context, L40S provide best embeddings perf per-dollar for large batch (fits larger batch sizes cheaply). H100 improves latency for very large context + quantized layers but increases $/unit — we recommend H100 only if you have strict single-request <120ms P95 for >8k contexts.

- Throughput/SLA guidance (conservative): 24 GPUs committed provides ~6k vectors/hr (with L40S-heavy batching for embeddings) and targeted 95th token latency ~160–200ms for our chat profile when routing policy pins low-latency requests to A100s. We’ll configure prefix caching and autoscale burst policy for peak windows.

- Discounts and commit: For a 6-month 24-GPU commit we can offer a 18% volume discount off list pricing + one month of burst credits (50 GPU-hours) to cover an initial ramp. To reach 22–25% we’d need a 12-month commitment or a guaranteed minimum spend (>$90k/month).

I’ve attached CloudMetrics_pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx with: per-GPU list price, effective price after the proposed 18% commit discount, sample monthly invoice, and an apples-to-apples perf/$ chart (A100 vs H100 vs L40S) tuned to your model families (generation and embeddings).

Below are the engineering notes (short):
- A100 80GB: best steady-state generative perf per-dollar for 2–4k contexts, predictable memory headroom for KV cache. Good for chat routes and long context retrieval.
- L40S 48GB: optimized for FP16 embeddings and large batch throughput; lower single-request throughput for long-context generation but much cheaper for batch embedding runs.
- H100: ~20–30% faster for some float kernels and larger context models but ~1.6–2x list price of A100; recommended only when latency SLOs are extremely tight and model families benefit from its Tensor Core optimizations.

If you’d like, we can run a short benchmark (48-hour) on a small representative subset of your prompts — we’ll need a sanitized prompt set and permission for a test run.

I’ll loop in pricing for the formal quote once you confirm the desired commit term.

Thanks — Jasmine
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: CloudMetrics_pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx
From: Anand Patel <anand.patel@cloudmetrics.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing & GPU options — follow up

Jasmine, Vivek —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the matrix — useful. Two clarifying items from Procurement:
1) Can the 18% be made 20% if we accept a short penalty-free termination window after month 3? Procurement wants some runway in case usage doesn't match projections.
2) For the burst credits you mentioned, can those be applied automatically (seamless burst) or do we need to request manual approval when we hit the commit limit?

Also we’d like to see a sample invoice that shows the blended GPU mix math (how you amortize A100 vs L40S in billing). Can you include a one-page example?

Thanks — Anand
Sr. Procurement Manager, CloudMetrics
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: FW: CloudMetrics — discount / termination ask

Team — forwarding CloudMetrics’ asks. Quick notes:
- We can make burst credits automatic up to the monthly credit allotment; beyond that they incur overage at the blended committed rate.
- We usually push back on termination windows for committed pools but can offer a pro-rated unwind (2-week notice) after month 3 with a 10% early-termination fee on remaining committed value. That helps protect our capacity planning.
- On the discount: Laura — can we flex to 20% for a 6-month if they take 26 GPUs instead of 24 (shift mix to 16 A100 + 10 L40S)? They’re price-sensitive and that additional 2 GPUs buys us buffer and amortization.

Asking for sign-off on the 20% special and the termination language. Rachel — can you draft the PDF invoice example (blended math) and I’ll include the SLA verbiage.

—Vivek
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CloudMetrics — discount / termination ask (Approved)

Vivek / team — approved with the following conditions:

1) Approve 20% off list pricing for a 6-month committed contract at 26 GPUs (16 x A100 80GB + 10 x L40S 48GB). This requires a signed PO by 2026-03-05 and a minimum monthly spend floor of $92,000.
2) Early unwind: pro-rated return after month 3 with a 10% unwind fee on remaining committed dollars. No full termination option.
3) Burst credits: auto-applied up to 60 GPU-hours/month; any additional burst billed at blended committed rate.
4) Include a 30-day benchmarking clause in the contract: if we run a benchmark and H100 shows >20% perf improvement for their exact workloads vs A100, we will offer a 12% rebate applied to months 1–3 to account for initial performance delta (not a hardware swap guarantee).

Rachel — please produce the one-page blended invoice sample and finalize SLA language using the numbers in Jasmine’s matrix. Jasmine — send the updated quote (with new 26-GPU mix, pricing, and the termination/unwind language) to Elena and CC procurement.

—Laura
Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
